scoring_methodology.relevance_labels: Manually assigned expected passage(s) per supported question as filename + chunk_id. Each short PDF yields exactly one passage (chunk_001), so passage-level and document-level recall are identical in this dataset; all expected passages/documents must occur in the top-k retrieved chunks.
scoring_methodology.retrieval_metric: Document-level Recall@5 (strict all-relevant-documents hit per question), measured only on supported questions.
scoring_methodology.answer_correctness: Deterministic required-keyword-group rubric declared in this script; every group must match and the response must not be a refusal.
scoring_methodology.grounding: A supported answer passes when it is correct, all labelled documents were retrieved, and citations name all labelled documents while naming no un-retrieved document.
scoring_methodology.unsupported_handling: Pass requires the canonical refusal text and llm_called=false.

limitations: The benchmark has only two short, single-page documents and twelve questions.
Relevance is labelled at document level, not passage-span level, because each PDF produces one chunk with the default settings.
Keyword scoring is deterministic and reproducible but is not a substitute for blinded human or semantic-judge evaluation.
Citation validity checks provenance labels, not full natural-language entailment of every generated clause.
The confidence value is the application's retrieval-strength heuristic, not calibrated answer probability.
